Results.ReviewText:
I always wanted a Weber grill. So for starters, I may be a little biased. As a Father’s Day gift in 1991, we bought my father a Genesis for Father’s Day. It was handed down to my brother and he still uses it to this day. I would consider myself to be way above average as a griller. I’ve been through two grills since being a homeowner, one used and one new (approx 10 years). Neither hold up to the quality that is my Weber. I also own a Kamado style grill, however I will not compare that to the weber as it is charcoal. As far as propane grills go, this is the best brand you can get. Remember you get what you pay for. My second grill was ok, however a powerful wind gust blew it over head over heels and dented it severely. I thoroughly clean my grilling apparatus 2x per year, and yet they still rusted. The Weber quality is clear as day. It is heavier. It is sturdier. The temp control is so sensitive that I recommend firing it up before your first cook just so you can get an understanding of 1) how hot this can get and 2) how you can micromanage the temperature down to every 5 degrees. 10 year warranty. They stand behind their grill. My next grill, if I ever need one, will be Weber. 
I’ve done 4 cooks on it and am very satisfied. If you can splurge on the cost, it will be money well spent. Why spend $200 every 5 years when you can spend $400 once? Finally some background on my grilling experience. I’ve done pork butts, ribs, steak, chicken, fish, brisket. Cold smoke, high sear, 6 racks of ribs at once. Believe me when I tell you, I’ve done al of those and will be trying them at some point on this Weber.
Results.Title: Longtime Griller, finally bought the Cadillac

About 10 - 12 years ago I had a Weber grill, similar in size ( three burners ) and found it to be really great.  I believe that this Spirit E-310 grill falls short of measuring up to the same standards.  What I have experienced is the following:
1.  I had problems with the burners lighting and called customer service.  They told me that I can no longer turn on the gas at the tank and then turn on and light the burners, but have to wait three to five minutes after the gas valve on the tank is opened.
2.  I find this grill is much more subject to flare-ups than my previous Weber grill.
3.  The metal on the E 310 is much more difficult, perhaps even impossible, to keep looking nice.
4.  The Spirit has two wheels for moving, but there is virtually no way to easily grasp the grill to lift the opposite end to move it.

The grill still grills food, but it just really is a little disappointing to me as I was basing the purchase on the previous grill, and this does fall somewhat short.

Results.ReviewText:
I bought this grill two months ago.  My wife insisted that I replace my fifteen year old Weber Genesis Silver series grill.  I think I cried a little, okay I cried a lot.  I loved that grill!

The functionality of the new grill itself is excellent.  It heats up fast and gets to a much higher temperature than my old Weber.  The heat distribution on the cooking surface is extraordinarily even.

I like to keep my grill in my garage, so I can grill throughout the New England winter.  This grill only has two wheels, which makes it difficult to move easily.  The side extensions are not part of the cart, so you can not grab the side table and move the grill.  They warp and bend.  You have to reach under the grill and grab the frame to move the grill.

Thank you for listening.  This was very therapeutic for me.  I am sure that I will learn to love my grill over time.

Results.ReviewText: I had a Weber Spirit from the 2000's that finally croaked so I purchased a new one. Its only okay. It takes a long time to get hot, 15 min or more. Results.Title: Very good cooking.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
After almost 21 years with my previous Weber Grill I finally had to break down and get a new grill. The Spirit II E-310 had the same cooking area as my old one so that was the grill for me. Easy to build (I always assemble things myself) and cooking on it has been a joy. Took a little time to get used to the burners going front to back as opposed to my old one that went from the right to the left, but that was easy to figure out. 
A few things that could be improved on: 
1) the chain for match lighting should have a couple of more hooks to keep it up under the left side tray and not hang down. 
2) there should be a way to lock the left side tray so that it is forever in the up position. It tends to lift a bit when you lift that side to move the grill. 
3) an option kit for installing wheels on the two left side legs. My old grill had wheels on those legs and it made moving the grill around very easy. They were lockable to preventit from moving when you didn't want it to move.

I'll probably figure a way to mount wheels and to permanently keep the left tray tightly in the up position, but for now, I'm enjoying bar-b-que-ing.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
After really wanting the Genesis II two burner, but that Weber was available anymore. I did more research on the Spirit II E-310 and I’m glad I did. Every review I read was positive, so I decided to buy it. I’ve never had a three burner grill. The extra burner has opened new grilling experiences for me, indirect grilling and cooking a whole meal at one time. 
The Spirit II was more than I ever thought it would be. It makes me want to grill everyday, as well as trying new things. 
Only one thing I wish was better and that’s a shorter axle for the wheels. The wheel cover pops off once a week. A shorter axle I think would help. But overall this is a great grill.
